rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which is either at-fault just cause or no-fault just cause. At-fault causes include nonpayment of rent, breach of a material lease term after written notice to correct, nuisance, waste, refusal to sign a substantially similar renewal, criminal activity, criminal threats, unauthorized assignment or sublet, refusal of lawful entry, unlawful use, failure of an employee-tenant to vacate after termination, and failure to deliver possession after giving notice. No-fault causes are owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order or local ordinance requiring vacating, and demolition or substantial remodel.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies of residential rental property (dwellings or units intended for human habitation, including in mobilehome parks) in San Diego; a tenancy means the right to occupy for more than 30 days and excludes fixed-term leases of three months or less.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or agreement-restricted affordable housing; housing subject to affordable housing subsidy agreements (not including Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and residential care facilities, adult residential facilities, non-profit transitional housing; school and college dormitories; property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with a landlord who lives there; single-family residence occupied by the landlord as principal residence (including renting up to two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs, and a mobilehome); two units in a single structure where the landlord occupies one; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property where the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management and tenants received the required written exemption notice.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.interaction_text: The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.

rules.title: Owner or relative move-in no-fault just cause
rules.requirement: An owner may terminate a tenancy in good faith to occupy the unit for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child, grandchild, parent, or grandparent for a minimum of 12 continuous months as a primary residence; for leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it. The intended occupant must move in within 90 days after the tenant vacates, the notice must name the intended occupant and relationship, and the ground does not apply if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a similar vacant unit exists.

rules.penalty: If the intended occupant does not occupy the unit within 90 days or for at least 12 continuous months, the owner shall offer the unit to the tenant who vacated it at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses in excess of any relocation assistance paid.
rules.quoted_span: The owner seeks to recover possession to occupy the residential rental property for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child (by blood or adoption), grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or grandparent for a minimum of 12 continuous months as that person’s primary residence.

rules.title: Demolition or substantial remodel no-fault just cause and notice
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy to demolish or substantially remodel, meaning permitted system work or hazardous-material abatement that cannot be done safely with the tenant in place and requires vacating for at least 30 continuous days. The landlord must post permit applications within three business days of submittal, secure permits before issuing notice, and give a written notice certified under penalty of perjury stating the intent, a right-to-re-rent statement, a description and expected duration with permits or contract, and why the tenant must vacate.
